tools.name: animation_camera_tracking
tools.description: Make the camera follow an animated entity or stop tracking to return control to user

track.description: true to track entity, false to stop tracking

animationId.description: Animation ID to track or untrack

tools.name: animation_control
tools.description: Start, pause, or resume animation playback

action.description: Action to perform: 'play' to start/resume, 'pause' to pause

tools.name: animation_create
tools.description: Create an animated entity with custom position samples. Provide positionSamples array with timing and coordinates.

height.description: Height in meters above WGS84 ellipsoid

items.description: Position sample at a specific time

positionSamples.description: Array of position samples with timing and coordinates

startTime.description: Animation start time (ISO 8601, defaults to first sample time)

stopTime.description: Animation stop time (ISO 8601, defaults to last sample time)

tools.name: animation_list_active
tools.description: Get a list of all active animations with their current states

tools.name: animation_remove
tools.description: Remove an animation and its associated entity

tools.name: animation_update_path
tools.description: Update the visual appearance of an existing animation path trail (lead/trail time, width, color)

tools.name: camera_fly_to
tools.description: Execute camera fly operation with advanced options like easing functions and callbacks

pitch.description: Pitch in degrees (-90 = down, 0 = horizon, 90 = up)

maximumHeight.description: Maximum height during flight in meters

pitchAdjustHeight.description: Height above ground to adjust pitch

flyOverLongitude.description: Longitude to fly over during flight

tools.name: camera_get_position
tools.description: Get comprehensive camera information including position, orientation, and view bounds

tools.name: camera_look_at_transform
tools.description: Lock the camera to look at a specific point on Earth, useful for orbiting around landmarks

offset.description: Camera offset from target (default: heading=0, pitch=-90°, range=1000m)

tools.name: camera_set_controller_options
tools.description: Configure camera movement constraints and behavior

enableCollisionDetection.description: Allow camera to go underground (default: true)

minimumZoomDistance.description: Minimum distance camera can zoom to surface

maximumZoomDistance.description: Maximum distance camera can zoom from surface

tools.name: camera_set_view
tools.description: Instantly set camera position and orientation without animation

pitch.description: Pitch in degrees (-90 = down, 0 = horizon, 90 = up)

tools.name: camera_start_orbit
tools.description: Start orbiting around the current look-at target

speed.description: Orbit speed in radians per second (default: 0.005)

tools.name: camera_stop_orbit
tools.description: Stop the current camera orbit animation

tools.name: cesium_disable_domain
tools.description: Disable a Cesium tool domain, hiding its tools from the tool list. Can be re-enabled later.

tools.name: cesium_enable_domain
tools.description: Enable a previously disabled Cesium tool domain, making its tools available again

tools.name: cesium_execute_code
tools.description: 当现有工具无法直接满足需求时，根据自然语言意图生成 CesiumJS 代码（经 grounding 生成、AST 安全校验、人工审批后，由前端主页面执行）。输入为用户意图描述，返回生成且通过安全校验的代码。

intent.description: 要完成的任务的自然语言描述（如：以上海为中心画一个半径 50 公里的圆）

description.description: 可选的补充说明（上下文、样式偏好等）

tools.name: cesium_list_domains
tools.description: List all available Cesium tool domains with their enabled/disabled status and tool counts

tools.name: clock_control
tools.description: Configure the global animation clock. Can set full configuration, just the current time, or just the multiplier

action.description: Action to perform: 'configure' for full clock setup, 'setTime' to change current time, 'setMultiplier' to change time rate

clock.description: Full clock configuration (required for 'configure' action). All times as ISO 8601 strings.

currentTime.description: Current time to set as ISO 8601 string (required for 'setTime' action, e.g., '2026-02-23T12:00:00Z')

multiplier.description: Time rate multiplier (required for 'setMultiplier' action, e.g., 1000 for 1000x real time)

tools.name: entity_add_billboard
tools.description: Create a billboard (image marker) entity at a specific location. Billboards are always screen-oriented and useful for icons and image markers. IMPORTANT: Always ask the user for an image URL before calling this tool, unless they already provided one. Do NOT invent or guess image URLs.

image.description: URL to image file (required) - can be external URL or data URI. IMPORTANT: Always ask the user for an image URL unless they provide one.

tools.name: entity_add_box
tools.description: Create a box entity at a specific location with customizable dimensions. Boxes are useful for representing buildings, containers, or volumetric data.

tools.name: entity_add_corridor
tools.description: Create a corridor entity along a path with specified width. Corridors are useful for representing roads, pipelines, routes, or paths.

positions.description: Array of positions defining corridor centerline

tools.name: entity_add_cylinder
tools.description: Create a cylinder or cone entity at a specific location. Cylinders are useful for representing towers, pillars, or volumetric structures.

tools.name: entity_add_ellipse
tools.description: Create an ellipse entity at a specific location with customizable appearance. Ellipses are useful for representing circular areas, zones, or coverage regions.

tools.name: entity_add_label
tools.description: Create a text label entity at a specific location. Labels are useful for annotations, names, and information display.

tools.name: entity_add_model
tools.description: Create a 3D model entity (glTF/GLB) at a specific location with orientation. Models are useful for buildings, vehicles, and complex 3D objects. IMPORTANT: Always ask the user for a model URL before calling this tool, unless they already provided one. Do NOT invent or guess model URLs.

uri.description: URI to glTF/GLB model file (required). IMPORTANT: Always ask the user for a model URL unless they provide one.

tools.name: entity_add_point
tools.description: Create a point entity at a specific location with customizable appearance. Use this to add markers, landmarks, or points of interest to the 3D scene.

tools.name: entity_add_polygon
tools.description: Create a polygon entity from an array of positions. Polygons are useful for areas, zones, and regions.

hierarchy.description: Array of positions defining polygon boundary

tools.name: entity_add_polyline
tools.description: Create a polyline entity connecting multiple positions. Polylines are useful for paths, routes, and connections.

positions.description: Array of positions defining polyline path

tools.name: entity_add_rectangle
tools.description: Create a rectangle entity defined by geographic bounds. Rectangles are useful for representing regions, bounding boxes, or areas of interest.

tools.name: entity_add_wall
tools.description: Create a wall entity from a series of positions with variable heights. Walls are useful for representing barriers, fences, or vertical structures.

positions.description: Array of positions defining wall path

tools.name: entity_list
tools.description: Get a list of all entities currently in the scene with their IDs, names, and types. Optionally filter by entity type or include detailed information.

includeDetails.description: Include detailed entity information (position, properties, etc.)

tools.name: entity_remove
tools.description: Remove an entity from the scene by ID or name pattern. Can remove a single entity or all matching entities.

entityId.description: The unique ID of the entity to remove

namePattern.description: Pattern to match entity names (if no ID provided)

removeAll.description: Remove all entities matching the criteria

tools.name: geolocation_geocode
tools.description: Convert an address, landmark, or place name to geographic coordinates. Use this for "What are the coordinates of X?" or "Where is X located?" queries. Examples: "Empire State Building", "Eiffel Tower", "1600 Pennsylvania Avenue", "Tokyo Tower", "Tokyo, Japan". Returns a SINGLE best matching location (not a list). DO NOT use for finding multiple businesses by category (use geolocation_search for "find restaurants", "find hotels", etc.).

address.description: SINGLE address, landmark, or place name to convert to coordinates. Examples: "Empire State Building", "Eiffel Tower", "1600 Pennsylvania Avenue", "Tokyo, Japan". Use this for "What are the coordinates of X?" queries. DO NOT use for finding multiple businesses (use geolocation_search instead).

countryCode.description: Optional two-letter country code to restrict search (e.g., 'US', 'GB', 'JP')

tools.name: geolocation_route
tools.description: Calculate optimal route between two locations with support for multiple travel modes (driving, walking, cycling, transit) and traffic awareness.

travelMode.description: Travel mode: driving, walking, cycling, or transit

tools.name: geolocation_search
tools.description: Search for MULTIPLE POIs by category or business type (e.g., "pizza restaurants", "gyms", "coffee shops", "hotels", "gas stations"). Use this for finding businesses and amenities, NOT for single landmarks. Returns MULTIPLE matching places. Supports both general search and location-based (nearby) search - use location + radius parameters for nearby searches like "gyms near Golden Gate Bridge". DO NOT use for "What are the coordinates of Empire State Building" or similar landmark queries - use geolocation_geocode instead. Supports location-biased search, radius filtering, and type filtering.

query.description: Category or TYPE of places to find (e.g., "pizza restaurants", "gyms", "coffee shops", "hotels", "gas stations"). Returns MULTIPLE places. DO NOT use for single landmarks like "Empire State Building" - use geolocation_geocode for those.

location.description: Center point for location-biased or nearby search. When combined with radius, performs a nearby search.

radius.description: Search radius in meters (max 50km). When specified with location, restricts results to this distance (nearby search). When omitted, results are biased toward location but not restricted.

types.description: Filter by place types (e.g., restaurant, cafe, hotel, hospital). Supported types vary by data source.

items.description: Type of place to search for (e.g., restaurant, cafe, hotel, hospital, fuel, bank, pharmacy, museum, library, park)

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results to return

tools.name: globe_set_lighting
tools.description: Enable or disable realistic globe lighting effects for day/night cycles

tools.name: imagery_add
tools.description: Add a new imagery layer to the globe. Supports various provider types including URL templates, WMS, WMTS, ArcGIS, Bing Maps, TMS, OpenStreetMap, Cesium Ion, and single tile providers.

type.description: Type of imagery provider to create

url.description: URL of the imagery service or tile template (not required for IonImageryProvider)

name.description: Display name for the imagery layer

tileMatrixSetID.description: Tile matrix set identifier (for WMTS providers)

maximumLevel.description: Maximum zoom level for the imagery layer

minimumLevel.description: Minimum zoom level for the imagery layer

show.description: Whether the layer is visible (default: true)

rectangle.description: Geographic extent to restrict the imagery layer

assetId.description: Cesium Ion asset ID (required for IonImageryProvider)

tools.name: imagery_list
tools.description: Get a list of all imagery layers currently on the globe with their indices, names, visibility, and provider types.

tools.name: imagery_remove
tools.description: Remove an imagery layer from the globe by index or name. Can remove a single layer or all non-base imagery layers.

index.description: Index of the imagery layer to remove

name.description: Name of the imagery layer to remove

tools.name: terrain_get
tools.description: Get information about the current terrain provider in the Cesium scene, including its source type, name, and configuration.

tools.name: terrain_remove
tools.description: Remove the current terrain provider and reset to the default WGS84 ellipsoid (flat globe with no terrain elevation data).

tools.name: terrain_set
tools.description: Set the terrain provider for the Cesium scene. Supports Cesium Ion terrain assets (type='ion'), direct terrain server URLs (type='url'), and WGS84 ellipsoid (type='ellipsoid') for a flat globe with no terrain. The default Cesium World Terrain can be loaded with type='ion' and assetId=1.

type.description: Source type: 'ion' for Cesium Ion assets, 'url' for direct terrain server URLs, 'ellipsoid' for flat WGS84 ellipsoid

assetId.description: Cesium Ion asset ID. Required when type is 'ion'

url.description: URL to a terrain server (e.g., quantized-mesh endpoint). Required when type is 'url'

name.description: Optional display name for the terrain provider

requestVertexNormals.description: Whether to request vertex normals for lighting. Default: true for ion/url

requestWaterMask.description: Whether to request water mask data for water effects. Default: false

requestMetadata.description: Whether to request terrain metadata. Default: true

tools.name: tileset_add
tools.description: Add a 3D Tiles tileset to the Cesium scene. Supports loading from Cesium Ion assets (type='ion') and direct tileset.json URLs (type='url'). Returns a tilesetId that can be used to remove the tileset later.

type.description: Source type for loading the 3D tileset. 'ion': Cesium Ion asset (assetId required). 'url': direct tileset.json URL (url required).

assetId.description: Cesium Ion asset ID. Required when type is 'ion'. Find asset IDs at https://ion.cesium.com/assets

url.description: URL of the tileset.json file. Required when type is 'url'. Example: https://example.com/tileset/tileset.json

name.description: Display name for the tileset. Used when listing or removing.

show.description: Whether the tileset is visible on load (default: true)

tools.name: tileset_list
tools.description: Get a list of all 3D tilesets currently loaded in the Cesium scene, including their IDs, names, source types, and visibility state. Use tilesetIds from this list with tileset_remove.

includeDetails.description: Include detailed source information for each tileset

tools.name: tileset_remove
tools.description: Remove a 3D tileset from the Cesium scene. Identify the tileset to remove by its tilesetId (returned by tileset_add), by name, or set removeAll=true to remove all loaded tilesets at once.

tilesetId.description: Unique tileset ID returned by tileset_add. Preferred removal method.

name.description: Display name of the tileset to remove

removeAll.description: Remove all loaded tilesets from the scene

tools.name: tileset_style
tools.description: Apply or update 3D Tiles styling (color and show conditions) on a loaded tileset. Target the tileset by tilesetId (from tileset_add) or by name. Use color for a single color expression, colorConditions for conditional coloring, show/showConditions for visibility rules. IMPORTANT: The 3D Tiles Styling expression language only supports color() with hex or named color strings (e.g. color('#ff0000'), color('red')). CSS functions like hsl(), rgb(), or rgba() are NOT supported and will silently fail. To create a color ramp based on a feature property (e.g. Height), always use colorConditions with discrete ranges instead of a single color expression. Example: colorConditions=[['${Height} >= 100', "color('#ff0000')"], ['true', "color('#00ff00')"]]

tilesetId.description: Unique tileset ID returned by tileset_add. Preferred targeting method.

name.description: Display name of the tileset to style

color.description: Cesium tile style color expression, e.g. "color('red')" or "color('${color}')". Applied as-is when colorConditions is not provided.

colorConditions.description: Array of [condition, color] pairs evaluated top-to-bottom. Each condition is a Cesium expression string; the first truthy one applies. Example: [["${height} >= 100", "color(\"blue\")"], ["true", "color(\"white\")"]]

show.description: Boolean or Cesium expression string to control feature visibility, e.g. true or "${height} > 10". Applied when showConditions is not provided.

showConditions.description: Array of [condition, show] pairs evaluated top-to-bottom. Example: [["${height} > 10", "true"], ["true", "false"]]
